result.scope_note: The congressional pay amendment (27th Amendment) was proposed in 1789 and ratified in 1992, a span of approximately 203 years. The original Bill of Rights (first ten amendments) were proposed in 1789 and ratified by 1791, a span of approximately 2 years. The claim asserts the former took longer, which is factually correct by recorded measurement.

excerpts.text: _See id._ On September 25, 1789, Congress proposed a similarly worded Congressional Pay Amendment.[14](https://constitution.congress.gov/browse/essay/amdt27-1/ALDE_00013830/#ALDF_00030056)Footnote
By the end of 1791, only six states had ratified the Congressional Pay Amendment.[17](https://constitution.congress.gov/browse/essay/amdt27-1/ALDE_00013830/#ALDF_00030059)Footnote

In 1873, the Ohio legislature ratified the Amendment to protest a congressional pay raise.[18](https://constitution.congress.gov/browse/essay/amdt27-1/ALDE_00013830/#ALDF_00030060)Footnote 
_See id._ Thereafter, the Amendment lay dormant until the late twentieth century when it was rediscovered by Gregory D.

_See id._ From the mid-1980s to the early 1990s, more than 30 state legislatures ratified the Amendment, responding to the American public’s opposition to congressional pay increases.[22](https://constitution.congress.gov/browse/essay/amdt27-1/ALDE_00013830/#ALDF_00030064)Footnote 
_See id._ The National Archivist proclaimed the Twenty-Seventh Amendment to have been ratified on May 7, 1992, more than two centuries after Congress had initially proposed it.[23](https://constitution.congress.gov/browse/essay/amdt27-1/ALDE_00013830/#ALDF_00030065)Footnote
